text:
The Wild's three-game winning streak ended 33 seconds into overtime, when Matthew Schaefer, the 2025 first overall pick, collected a pass from Jean-Gabriel Pageau and beat Jesper Wallstedt for his second goal of the night. Schaefer, a defenseman, also assisted on Bo Horvat's power-play goal and played 30:00, finishing with six shots on goal. A year ago he was in the Ontario Hockey League with the Erie Otters. Now he is deciding NHL games.

The numbers say the Islanders earned it, though not by much. Our model gives NYI a 58% chance of winning if this game were replayed many times, built on 2.74 expected goals (the quality of their chances) to 2.31 for MIN. The Islanders dominated the second period, out-chancing the Wild 0.96 to 0.38. Minnesota answered with Quinn Hughes' backhand late in that period, a shot we gave a 1% chance of going in, and Matt Boldy tied it at 3-3 with just under four minutes left in regulation. Wallstedt allowed about 1.3 more goals than his 26 shots against should have produced, while Ilya Sorokin also finished below expectation, allowing about 0.7 more than the chances against him deserved. MIN also gave the puck away 23 times to NYI's 16.

Minnesota now has to start a new streak after the three straight wins ended. The Islanders leave with a win built on their top young defenseman. We'd watch whether Schaefer's workload holds up, since 30 minutes a night is a lot for any player.
